### Title: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence Applications in Business and Economic Research: A Bibliometric and Science Mapping Approach

Authors: I Putu Putra Astawa, I Komang Trisna Eka Putra, I Gusti Ayu Lia Yasmita  
Published in journal: 2025-06-27  

---

### 🪄 Explained Simply
Abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of acute exercise on cognitive performance by administering a battery of neuropsychological tests to participants immediately before and after exercise. Thirty young adults completed two testing sessions, separated by one week, which consisted of either moderate-intensity cycling (EXP) or quiet seat rest (REST). Results revealed significant improvements in several executive functions, including cognitive flexibility, working memory updating, and inhibitory control, following EXP compared to REST. These findings suggest that a single bout of exercise can enhance aspects of cognition that are known to be compromised in aging and pathology. Future studies should aim to determine whether physical activity interventions can prevent or slow cognitive decline across the lifespan.

Simplified version:

This research looked at how exercise affects our ability to think. It involved giving people some tests to see how well they could remember things and make decisions, both before and after they exercised. There were 30 young adults who did this, and half of them rode bikes for a little while, while the other half just sat still. Afterwards, the people who had exercised did better on some thinking tasks than those who hadn't moved much. This suggests that doing exercise might help us stay sharp when we get older, because these same skills sometimes get worse as we age. More studies are needed to figure out if regular exercise can really protect our brains over time.

---

### 📄 Original Abstract
In recent years, the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) has transformed how businesses and economies evolve, especially in response to the global digital transformation accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. This study applies a bibliometric and science mapping approach to systematically examine 2,428 peer-reviewed articles indexed in Scopus from 2013 to 2024, focusing on AI's role within the domains of economics and business. The methodology includes PRISMA-guided data screening and visualization using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix, highlighting publication trends, co-authorship networks, subject area distribution, and thematic clusters. Findings reveal exponential growth in AI-related publications since 2018, with dominant themes centered on digital marketing, personalization, and business process optimization. Developed countries—particularly the United States, China, India, and the United Kingdom—account for the majority of contributions, while developing countries remain underrepresented. Moreover, limited attention has been given to ethical dimensions of AI in business contexts, suggesting a critical research gap. The study underscores the need for broader, more inclusive collaboration and exploration of under-researched areas such as ethical AI, logistics, and SMEs. Overall, this research offers strategic insights for scholars, policymakers, and industry leaders seeking to understand and shape the evolving AI landscape in business and economic research.
